canonical_name: APPS (Automated Programming Progress Standard; 'Measuring Coding Challenge Competence With APPS', Hendrycks et al.)
metric: strict accuracy (% of problems whose generated program passes all test cases; reported per difficulty and averaged over the 5,000-problem test set); secondary: test case average
abandoned_evidence: Last report by any of the 9 labs: Claude 3 model card 2024-03-04 (APPS 0-shot 70.2%); no lab reports in the following 30 months to the cutoff. No official leaderboard exists (GitHub repo hendrycks/apps has none); the community Papers-with-Code leaderboard was shut down in 2025-07 (archive only), and surviving mirrors (e.g., https://www.codesota.com/benchmark/apps) show no entries after 2023.
score_at_release_system: GPT-Neo 2.7B fine-tuned, top-1 strict accuracy averaged over test set (test case average 10.15%)
lineage: APPS (2021-05; problems from Codewars, AtCoder, Kattis, Codeforces etc.; 1,000 introductory / 3,000 interview / 1,000 competition test problems) -> used by Codex (2021-07), AlphaCode (2022-02, which introduced CodeContests); later code-contest successors TACO (2023) and LiveCodeBench (2024-03).
best_by_cutoff: 70.2 - Claude 3 Opus, 0-shot, 2024-03-04 (self-report; subset/metric not specified in model card; https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/de8ba9b01c9ab7cbabf5c33b80b7bbc618857627/Model_Card_Claude_3.pdf)
notes: No human baseline in the paper -> criterion B, threshold 90% strict accuracy on the full 5,000-problem test set. No result >=90 found by 2026-09-30; most published scaffold results (MapCoder, CodeSim, LPW etc.) use small APPS subsets, not the official test split. Lab reports are split by difficulty or unspecified (Codex-12B filtered pass@1 intro 22.78 / interview 2.64 / competition 3.0; Code Llama 34B intro pass@5 32.81; Claude 3 Opus 70.2 0-shot, split unspecified). APPS remains in academic use (incl. as RL training data), but under the codebook definition (>=12 months without lab reports AND without leaderboard activity/closure) it is abandoned; abandoned_date set to the last lab report because the Papers-with-Code archive could not be queried (HF datasets-server timed out) - if a later PwC leaderboard entry exists (e.g., 2024-2025 scaffold papers), abandoned_date should move to that month. Known test-case insufficiency/false positives in APPS (discussed in the AlphaCode paper) not coded as E: no lab publicly stopped reporting because of an audit.

canonical_name: ASDiv (Academia Sinica Diverse MWP Dataset, 'A Diverse Corpus for Evaluating and Developing English Math Word Problem Solvers', Miao et al., ACL 2020)
release_source: https://aclanthology.org/2020.acl-main.92/ (ACL 2020, July 2020); dataset 'upload ASDiv v1.0' commit 2020-07-30 in https://github.com/chaochun/nlu-asdiv-dataset (arXiv copy 2106.15772 only in 2021-06)
ab_system: Faithful CoT with GPT-4 as translator + deterministic solver (Lyu et al.)
ab_mode: few-shot, greedy decoding; LM writes reasoning chain/program executed by external solver (Python)
ab_source: https://github.com/veronica320/Faithful-COT (README commit 1c883aa, 2023-05-02 'Add new results summary for GPT4 and ChatGPT': GPT-4 ASDiv 95.6); paper https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.13379
strict_system: GPT-4 with CoT prompting (no tools), evaluated in the ToRA paper (third party to OpenAI)
strict_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.17452 (ToRA, v1 2023-09; Table 2: GPT-4 CoT 91.3, GPT-4 PAL 92.6 on ASDiv, 2,215 test examples)
score_at_release_system: UnitDep (statistical MWP solver), 5-fold cross-validation on full ASDiv (LCA++ 36, GTS 36; ASDiv-A subset best 78)
lineage: Built in response to earlier MWP corpora (MAWPS, Math23K-style); ASDiv-A arithmetic subset (used to build SVAMP, 2021-03); used in CoT-era LLM evaluations (Wei et al. CoT 2022-01, PaLM 2022-04, PAL 2022-11, Toolformer 2023-02, Llama 2 2023-07, DeepSeek-Coder PAL 2023-11).
best_by_cutoff: 95.6 - Faithful CoT + GPT-4 (2023-05, self, scaffold with solver); best tool-free found: GPT-4 CoT 91.3 (ToRA, 2023-09). Not exhaustively searched beyond 2024 (benchmark dropped from lab reports after 2023-11).
notes: No human baseline in the paper (only says SOTA systems are 'not competitive with human performance') -> criterion B, threshold 90. No official test split: the paper used 5-fold CV; LLM papers evaluate on the whole set or filtered versions (2,096 in CoT-style setups; 2,215 in ToRA). AB coded in main mode with a solver-backed scaffold because ASDiv's protocol (MWP solvers that output equations/answers) does not exclude computation tools; if tools were excluded, the first >=90 tool-free result found is GPT-4 CoT 91.3 (2023-09). Pre-GPT-4 bests were below 90 (e.g., code-davinci-002 with self-consistency/verifiers ~88). Strict: ToRA's paper does not state explicitly that its GPT-4 numbers are its own runs, but they are not OpenAI numbers (third-party), so treated as independent. Lab reports end 2023-11 (DeepSeek Coder PAL 76.7).

Earlier >=9.0 results not found (official leaderboard max 8.38; lab self-reports <=8.27 before 2025). v1.1 treated as the same unit (same 683 queries/protocol; ~22% of reference answers corrected by the maintainers on 2024-06-15) - labs mix v1.0 (DeepSeek, Qwen2) and v1.1 (Qwen2.5, Qwen3) numbers. The maintainers' own reference-answer correction is not an E(iii) audit.

abandoned_evidence: Last lab reports: Kimi K2 GitHub README 2025-07-11 and Kimi K2 tech report 2025-07-28 (89.5); none in the following 14 months (Kimi-K2-Instruct-0905 card has no AutoLogi). Official leaderboard = static README table in https://github.com/8188zq/AutoLogi (last README update 2025-05-06; repo inactive since).
score_at_release_system: Claude-3.5-Sonnet overall (EN 72.53, CN 68.24); GPT-4o EN 72.61 - official README leaderboard / paper
lineage: Synthesized from multiple-choice logic datasets AR-LSAT and LogiQA (program verifiers + traversal functions); companion training set released; used mainly by Qwen (Qwen3 tech report) and Moonshot (Kimi K2).
best_by_cutoff: 89.8 - Claude Sonnet 4 (w/o extended thinking), third-party run in Kimi K2 README (2025-07-11); self-reports: Kimi K2 Instruct 89.5 (2025-07), Qwen3-235B-A22B thinking 89.0 (2025-05-14)
notes: No human baseline (three human evaluators only validated the verifier) -> criterion B, threshold 90. No result >=90 found by the cutoff; lab-reported numbers do not state whether they are EN, CN or overall (Qwen3 table: o1 79.8, DeepSeek-R1 86.1, Gemini 2.5 Pro 85.4, Qwen3-235B 89.0; Kimi K2 table: DeepSeek-V3-0324 88.9, GPT-4.1 88.2, Claude Opus 4 86.1) - the benchmark is close to the threshold, so a later unreported >=90 cannot be excluded. canonical_name: BIG-Bench Hard (BBH): 23 challenging BIG-Bench tasks ('Challenging BIG-Bench Tasks and Whether Chain-of-Thought Can Solve Them', Suzgun et al.)
metric: exact-match accuracy averaged over 23 tasks (usually 3-shot CoT)
ab_source: https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/fed9cc193a14b84131812372d8d5857f8f304c52/Model_Card_Claude_3_Addendum.pdf (Claude 3.5 Sonnet addendum, June 2024; Table 1: 'BIG-Bench Hard ... 3-shot CoT 93.1%'); release https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-3-5-sonnet
c_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.19187 (BIG-Bench Extra Hard, v1 2025-02-26; Google DeepMind; co-authors include BBH authors Yi Tay and Quoc V. Le)
c_quote: "State-of-the-art models achieve near-perfect scores on many tasks in BBH, thus diminishing its utility" (abstract); body: state-of-the-art models 'achieve over 90% accuracy' on BBH, making it 'less effective in discriminating between the reasoning abilities of the latest generation of LLMs'; "BBEH replaces each task in BBH with a novel task that probes a similar reasoning capability"
score_at_release_system: Codex (code-davinci-002), 3-shot CoT, all-task average (answer-only 56.6; InstructGPT CoT 68.4; PaLM 540B CoT 63.3 in v1 Table 3)
lineage: Parent: BIG-Bench (2022-06, arXiv 2206.04615); BBH (2022-10) -> successor BIG-Bench Extra Hard (BBEH, 2025-02, replaces each BBH task citing saturation). Open LLM Leaderboard v2 (2024-06) uses a normalized BBH variant.
best_by_cutoff: 93.2 - Claude 3.5 Sonnet (new), 3-shot CoT, 2024-10-22 (self-report); best base-model self-report: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-Base 90.98 (2026-02-16)
notes: Average human-rater 67.7 < 85 -> criterion B, threshold 90. First >=90 found: Claude 3.5 Sonnet 93.1 (3-shot CoT, 2024-06); before that the best were Gemini 1.5 Pro (May 2024) 89.2, Claude 3 Opus 86.8 (2024-03), Gemini Ultra 83.6 (2023-12). Lab reports continue to 2026-09 mostly for BASE models (3-shot, often answer-only/EM), where scores stay <91 - base and chat/CoT numbers are not comparable. Strict event not established: no organizer leaderboard; I could not find a dated independent single-model run >=90 (Open LLM Leaderboard v2 uses a normalized, non-CoT variant with much lower scores; web search budget exhausted). C coded as judgement call: BBEH is by Google DeepMind with two of the eleven BBH authors and explicitly cites saturation as reason for replacing each BBH task; treat as C only if partial creator overlap is accepted.

canonical_name: BioLP-bench: Measuring understanding of biological lab protocols by LLMs (I. Ivanov)
release_source: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.08.21.608694v3 (bioRxiv DOI dated 2024-08-21; v3 2024-09-12); code/data https://github.com/baceolus/BioLP-bench (initial commit 2024-08-09)
metric: accuracy (%) at identifying the introduced mistake in a lab protocol (LLM-graded open-ended answer)
human_baseline: 38.4 (human experts on a random subset of tasks)
score_at_release_system: GPT-4o (Mistral Large 16; most other models ~7), bioRxiv paper
lineage: Protocol-troubleshooting format similar to LAB-Bench ProtocolQA (OpenAI system cards describe it as 'similar in format to ProtocolQA Open-Ended'); used in OpenAI (o1, o3-mini, deep research, GPT-4.5) and xAI (Grok 4 family) preparedness/bio-risk evaluations.
best_by_cutoff: 47 - Grok 4 (API), xAI model card 2025-07-09 (self-report, 0.47); OpenAI best o1-preview 36 (o1 system card 2024-12-05)
notes: Expert baseline 38.4% < 85% of scale -> criterion B, threshold 90 (models already exceed the expert average: Grok 4 47, but that is not an event under the rules). 800 test cases from 11 protocols, mistakes introduced into published protocols (curation: expert-written protocols with synthetic error insertion). No result near 90 by the cutoff. Last lab report 2025-11-17 (Grok 4.1 Thinking 0.37), i.e. <12 months before the cutoff -> alive, not abandoned. Dual-use bio capability eval but measures capability, so main stratum.

n_items: 90 (v11, 2026-07: 73 human-solvable + 17 human-hard; 99 at public release v8)
lineage: Internal Anthropic eval first reported in Claude Opus 4.6 system card (2026-02, 'not publicly released', 61.5%) -> 'BioMysteryBench Verified' (Opus 4.7, 2026-04-16) -> public gated HF release v8 (2026-04-28, 99 problems) -> v11 (2026-07-06, 90 problems after June-2026 expert audit: 9 removed, 24 edited, grading rule clarified). Also reported by Google (Gemini 3.7/3.8 Flash, self-computed) and Tencent (Hy4 preview).
best_by_cutoff: 90.1 - Claude Opus 5, Human Solvable, 2026-07-24 (self); later: Claude Opus 5.5 89.3 (2026-09-22, self), Gemini 3.8 Flash 88.8 (2026-09-02, Google self-computed), Claude Sonnet 5 87.5 (as listed by Google)
notes: Birth set to the public dataset release (2026-04-28/29); the benchmark existed earlier as an internal eval (Opus 4.6 system card 2026-02 states these evaluations are 'not publicly released'), so before 2026-04 it would be excluded:internal. Human Solvable subset is defined by human success -> degenerate baseline -> criterion B, threshold 90. Metric changed over time (full set 61.5 in 2026-02; Verified/Hard in 2026-04; Human Solvable/Human Difficult from 2026-05), and v11 removed 9 and edited 24 of 99 problems (>10% of items touched) - could be treated as a new version; AB coded on the v11-era Human Solvable metric. Opus 5's 90.1 is barely above threshold and not independently verified (strict: none; Google ran only Gemini and GPT-5.6 Terra itself). The June 2026 audit was done by the creators themselves, so not E(iii). Opus 5 system card not fetched directly (value from lab-report input and llm-stats).

canonical_name: BixBench: a Comprehensive Benchmark for LLM-based Agents in Computational Biology (FutureHouse)
metric: open-answer accuracy (%) of an agent analysing the data capsule in a notebook environment, graded by string/range/LLM verifiers (primary); multiple-choice accuracy with/without refusal option is secondary
score_at_release_system: best frontier model (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) open-answer accuracy, arXiv v1 abstract; MCQ 'no better than random' (v3 text: Claude 3.5 Sonnet 21 vs GPT-4o 15)
n_items: 205 open-answer questions over 61 capsules (dataset v1.5; v1 had ~300 questions over 50+ capsules)
lineage: BixBench v1 (2025-02, ~300 questions) -> v1.5 dataset (205 questions/61 capsules; paper v3 2025-10). Related FutureHouse LAB-Bench (2024). Used in OpenAI (GPT-Rosalind, GPT-5.5) and xAI (Grok 4.5-4.7) release materials.
best_by_cutoff: 80.5 - GPT-5.5, 2026-04-23 (OpenAI self-report, setting not stated; https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-5-5/); xAI reports 93.8 for Grok 4.5/4.6 but in 'zero-shot MCQ accuracy' mode (secondary metric)
notes: No human baseline (authors list it as future work) -> criterion B, threshold 90 on the primary open-answer metric. No open-answer result >=90 found. xAI's Grok 4.5 (2026-07-16) and Grok 4.6 (2026-08-12) 93.8% are explicitly 'zero-shot MCQ' - a secondary mode, so not coded as AB; if MCQ results were accepted, AB would be 2026-07 (xAI self-report). OpenAI's 80.5 does not state mode/version. Item set changed between v1 (~296 questions) and v1.5 (205 questions), which may warrant a separate unit; labs do not say which version they use. Last lab report 2026-09-21 -> alive.

The official leaderboard (JS-rendered) could not be read, and Chinese-model leaderboard submissions >=90 may predate 2024-06 -> date_upper_bound=1.
